analysis.title: US Data Center Capacity update: Framing risks to our data center forecasts
key_insights: Counting only data centers already under construction, US net additions are 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29 (1.5 PUE, Aterio data). GS forecasts are 20/24/23 GW-IT, so 2027 and 2028 are covered by projects already being built.
GS calls its forecasts appropriately conservative and acknowledges they have likely been below consensus expectations.

The US has 57 GW-gross of active data center capacity, with 9 GW-gross more under construction for 65 GW-gross by end of 2026. Another 78 GW-gross is under construction beyond 2026, with net additions of 33/37/8/0 GW-gross for 2027/28/29/30, which GS treats as low-risk.
For 2029 the under-construction pipeline (5 GW-IT) is far below the GS forecast (23 GW-IT). Hitting that forecast depends on announced projects that have not yet started construction.

Investors have pushed back that upstream compute measures such as CoWoS capacity imply more data center capacity is needed. Aterio sees an additional 137 GW-gross of high-likelihood announced capacity for 2027-30, based on permitting, financing and power secured. GS sees announced-but-not-started projects as higher execution risk on timing and prefers project-by-project evaluation.
Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan are about 42% of under-construction and announced high-likelihood capacity. Texas alone is 26%.

On under-construction projects only, Texas is 20% of 2027E net additions and 27% of 2028E net additions. The Texas Governor-elect (Gina Hinojosa) has called for an immediate moratorium on data centers.

GS says moratoriums are not bans or cancellations. The main risks are delayed ready-for-service dates (which could cause some contract cancellations), higher financing costs from longer construction, higher taxes from reduced tax breaks, and higher capex for transmission and generation to limit ratepayer impact.

A moratorium would likely apply to new data centers, not those under construction. Aterio counts site work (land clearing, grading, trenching, foundations) as under construction, so a moratorium could still hit sites with site work but no electricity services agreement or environmental and air permits.
IREN (Neutral) has the highest Texas exposure in GS coverage, with 73%/87% of its data center capacity in the state.
DLR (Buy) and EQIX (Neutral) have minimal exposure to the development-heavy markets because they focus on tier 1 and tier 2 markets and smaller, non-AI footprints.
CLS (Buy, Conviction List) and ANET (Buy) would be hurt by data center delays, since AI infrastructure drives server (CLS) and data center ethernet switch (CLS and ANET) growth.

risk_factors: State-level data center moratoriums, most acutely in Texas, delaying ready-for-service dates and possibly causing contract cancellations.
Higher financing costs from longer construction times.
Higher taxes from reduced data center tax breaks.
Higher capex for transmission and generation infrastructure to limit impact on other ratepayers.
Under-construction sites that have site work but no electricity services agreement or environmental and air permits could be caught by a moratorium.
Announced-but-not-started capacity, which drives 2028 upside and 2029-30, carries higher execution and timing risk.
charts_described: Exhibit 4 shows 2026-30 cumulative net additions by state: Texas 57,041 GW-gross units in MW (26%), Ohio 15,009 (7%), Georgia 12,204 (5%), Nevada 7,171 (3%), Michigan 2,451 (1%), Other 129,206 (58%).

Exhibit 1 shows US data center capacity rising from 65 GW-gross in 2026 to 143 GW-gross by 2030 on active and under-construction capacity only, with net additions of 33/37/8/0 GW-gross in 2027/28/29/30.
Exhibit 2 shows announced capacity tagged high likelihood by Aterio adding 3/35/61/38 GW-gross to 2027/28/29/30.
geopolitical: Several US gubernatorial races flipped from Republican to Democratic, with campaigns in Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan (D-incumbent) featuring stricter data center regulation.
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for an immediate moratorium on data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Under-construction projects alone give 22/24 GW-IT of net additions for 2027/28 against GS forecasts of 20/24 GW-IT. Upstream compute measures such as CoWoS capacity suggest more capacity is needed, and Aterio sees 137 GW-gross of high-likelihood announced capacity for 2027-30.
tension_points.bear_case: Moratoriums in Texas and other states could delay ready-for-service dates, raise financing costs and taxes, and force higher infrastructure capex. Announced-but-not-started capacity carries higher timing risk, and under-construction capacity covers only 5 GW-IT in 2029 against a GS forecast of 23 GW-IT.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moratorium reaching projects that have done site work but lack an electricity services agreement or environmental and air permits, which would hit 2027-28 under-construction net additions.
